Tax, the oncoprotein of human T-cell leukemia virus type 1, activates CREB and NF-κB pathways in HTLV- 1 infected cells, and that these two pathways contribute to HTLV-1-infected cell resistance to apoptosis.
Tax activates CREB in HTLV- 1 infected cells, that CREB activation is important for Tax anti-apoptotic function, and that CREB activation contributes to HTLV-1 immortalization.

the identification of the molecular mechanisms involved in the survival of HTLV-1 transformed cells and the development of new strategies for the treatment of HTLV- 1-associated diseases.
the study of the molecular mechanisms used by the HTLV-1 oncoprotein Tax to induce cell transformation.
the molecular mechanisms involved in HTLV- 1 infection and its associated diseases, with a particular focus on Tax.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NF-κB and CREB signaling pathways are both involved in Tax-induced anti-apoptotic effect, but with different levels of importance depending on the cell type and the apoptotic stimuli.
the anti-apoptotic effect of Tax is multifactorial and is not restricted to the activation of the NF-κB signaling pathway, but rather involves the activation of other pathways such as CREB.
both NF-κB and CREB activation by Tax play important roles in the antiapoptotic effect of Tax.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Tax activates the NF-κB and CREB pathways in HTLV- 1-infected cells, which are both important in cell survival.
CREB and NF-κB pathways can be used by Tax to induce cell survival, but the relative contribution of each pathway to the anti-apoptotic effect of HTLV-1 is still unclear.
Tax activates CREB and CREB-dependent transcription, and CREB activation by Tax may play a role in HTLV- 1-induced leukemogenesis and/or in the resistance of HTLV-1-infected cells to death.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CREB activation is an important mechanism of survival in HTLV- 1 infected cells, and that Tax can act as a CREB survival factor.
Tax has a complex role in the control of cell survival and that its effect may be dependent on the cellular environment.
